text:
maria: heads up — after the exporter rollout at 03:00 we saw a noticeable CPU uptick on the telemetry workers and p99 token latency in the runtime jumped ~95ms. @priya can you take a look?
priya: saw the alert. looking at flamegraphs now. quick guess: per-span protobuf size increased after retaining more attributes in the ingest pipeline.
aj: do we have a histogram of span payload sizes pre/post? that'd tell us whether it's bytes or CPU from encoding.
dan: I pulled traces for one worker — median span size went from ~420B to ~1.1KB. serialization cost + more copies seems plausible.
maria: ok that matches. curious if exporting more small spans is worse than batching fewer larger envelopes. can we try an aggregation prototype that bundles spans into a single export message to reduce per-RPC overhead?
priya: yeah, i put together a quick variant: it aggregates spans by trace_id modulo N into a single WriteRequest, keeps original span identities but collapses per-span overhead. config snippet:```yaml
telemetry:
  exporter:
    mode: aggregated
    agg_bucket_count: 8
    max_bytes_per_batch: 256KB
    attribute_prune: default
```
luke: nice. can we toggle it on one node? also want to test with attribute_prune=aggressive to check CPU vs quality tradeoff.
aj: i'll spin up a canary with agg_bucket_count=8 and prune=default; will route 2% of telemetry for 30min. starting now.
telemetry-bot: canary deployment started on worker-7 (id: w-7). routing rule applied: telemetry.route=canary-agg.
dan: early numbers after 5m: worker-7 CPU down 12% vs baseline, exporter RPC count down 58%, but average exported envelope size up ~2.6x. p99 export latency decreased ~80ms for runtime requests that hit that worker.
priya: promising. quick caveat: aggregation increases memory transiently due to batching window, and we might delay span visibility by ~50-100ms depending on flush interval.
maria: for most dashboards ~100ms is fine but for some low-latency traces it's not. we should measure tail latency for affected product routes.
aj: ran a synthetic job hitting low-latency route; p99 runtime latency improved 60ms, but end-to-end trace visibility delay 120ms (measured by event timestamp).
dan: CPU savings are real though — extrapolates to ~18% cluster CPU reduction if we roll to 100% with these params.
luke: what about sampling instead of aggregation? that lowers cost but loses coverage. aggregation preserves fidelity but changes timing.
priya: agreed. plan: 1) run 5% canary across a few workload shapes (batch, interactive) for 4h with agg_bucket_count in {4,8,16} and attribute_prune={default,aggressive}; 2) capture CPU, p50/p95/p99 runtime latency, exporter RPCs, and visibility delay; 3) PR a rollout path with config flags + telemetry insights.
maria: sounds good. @aj can you open the canary matrix and add dashboards for visibility-delay and envelope-sizes? link the PR once ready.
aj: on it — will post dashboard links here. starting the expanded canary now. :rocket:
telemetry-bot: canary matrix job queued: job id tm-2026-174.
priya: quick note — if aggregation reduces write amplification to our S3/archiver it will also lower downstream costs. include archived bytes metric in the report.
dan: added archived_bytes and exporter_rpc_count to the canary SLO widgets.
maria: thanks all. if results look like the early run, we should do a 5%->25% ramp with a rollback hook on visibility_delay > 300ms or runtime_p99 regress > 25ms.
luke: +1. also document compatibility with our ingest contract (no semantic changes to spans).
aj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/612 — contains prototype and perf numbers from w-7.
priya: I'll run the aggressive prune job after this batch and post a diff of QA on sampling vs aggregation.
maria: great. we'll reconvene in #eng-platform after the 4h run. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
